Elastic-net feature selection with tuned alpha and lambda

Source: R/fs_elastic.R
fs_elastic.Rd

Tunes an elastic-net model over a grid of alpha and lambda values with caret::train(method = "glmnet") and selects the predictors whose coefficient is non-zero at the winning pair. Handles regression (numeric outcome) and classification (factor, character or logical outcome).

Usage

fs_elastic(
  data,
  target,
  alpha_seq = seq(0.1, 1, by = 0.1),
  lambda_seq = NULL,
  trControl = NULL,
  metric = NULL,
  use_pca = FALSE,
  nPCs = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  verbose = FALSE,
  n_cores = 1L
)

Arguments

data

A data frame (or data.table) containing the target and the candidate predictors, with unique, non-empty column names.

target

Single string naming the outcome column in data.

alpha_seq

Numeric vector of alpha values to tune over, each in [0, 1]. Default seq(0.1, 1, by = 0.1), which leaves out 0 (ridge) because ridge cannot zero a coefficient.

lambda_seq

Numeric vector of non-negative lambda values to tune over, or NULL (default) to use glmnet's own path at each alpha (see "Tuning grid and metrics").

trControl

Optional caret::trainControl() object; a partial list or a string is an error. If NULL (default), 5-fold CV with an NA-safe summary function is used. When use_pca = TRUE, pcaComp = nPCs is added to its preProcOptions. Its allowParallel is always overwritten with n_cores > 1, so a registered foreach backend is used only when n_cores > 1.

metric

Optional character. Performance metric to optimize. If NULL (default), "RMSE" for regression and "Accuracy" for classification. If caret does not find the name in the summary output, it warns and falls back to its default, and details$metric_name reports the metric actually used.

use_pca

Logical; default FALSE. Whether to project the predictors onto principal components inside each resample.

nPCs

Integer >= 1. Number of principal components to retain when use_pca = TRUE; must be strictly less than min(nrow, ncol) of the predictor matrix. Default NULL, which is an error when use_pca = TRUE and ignored otherwise.

seed

Optional whole number; default NULL, which leaves the RNG alone. When given, the seed is set for this call only and the previous RNG state is restored on exit. The resampling folds are drawn in the main R process and the glmnet fits are deterministic, so a seeded n_cores > 1 run gives the same result as a seeded sequential one. When trControl$seeds is unset (NA, the trainControl() default), caret draws one seed per resample from this seed in the main process and sets it on each worker, so seeded runs that use worker-side randomness (for example sampling = "up") are reproducible with any n_cores. A user-supplied trControl$seeds takes precedence.

verbose

Logical; default FALSE. Print progress messages.

n_cores

Integer >= 1; default 1 (sequential, and no cluster is created). Number of workers for parallel training; values above the detected core count are capped. Values above 1 need the 'foreach' and 'doParallel' packages.

Value

An fs_result object with:

selected

Columns (or components, when use_pca = TRUE) whose coefficient at the chosen alpha/lambda is non-zero; for multinomial fits, the union across classes.

scores

Named numeric vector of absolute coefficients at the chosen alpha/lambda, one entry per column the model saw; columns shrunk to zero are kept with a score of 0. NULL for multinomial fits, where a predictor has one coefficient per class and no single score exists.

method

"elastic_net".

task

"regression" or "classification".

model

The caret::train object.

details

List of coef (coefficients at the winning lambda, intercept included: a sparse matrix, or a list of them for multinomial fits), best_alpha and best_lambda (the winning tuning pair), metric_name (the metric caret optimized, which differs from metric when caret fell back to its default), metric_value (its resampled value for the winning pair, NA when the metric is absent from caret's results table; optimistic, see Details), use_pca, and n_features (number of columns the model saw, which is nPCs when use_pca = TRUE).

call

The matched call.

Details

The elastic net penalizes coefficients with a mix of an L1 (lasso) and an L2 (ridge) penalty: alpha sets the mix and lambda the overall strength. Both are chosen by resampling, and every column with a non-zero coefficient at the winning pair is reported. When the winning alpha is below 1, the ridge part spreads weight across correlated predictors, so a group of collinear columns tends to survive together instead of being reduced to one representative as fs_lasso() tends to do.

alpha = 0 is pure ridge, which never sets a coefficient to exactly zero and so cannot select. The default alpha_seq starts at 0.1 for that reason. If you include 0 and it wins, every column is selected and a warning says so.

The winning pair is the one with the best resampled metric (caret's default selectionFunction = "best"). With hundreds of alpha/lambda candidates that choice is noisy and leans towards too little penalty: on pure-noise data (100 rows, 50 predictors) it selected 8.5 predictors on average and at least one in every run. A trControl with selectionFunction = "oneSE" picks the most penalized pair within one standard error of the best and was much sparser in the same simulation (1.8 predictors on average).

For the same reason details$metric_value, the best value over the whole grid, is an optimistic estimate of performance. fs_elastic() holds out no test rows and reports no honest performance estimate; that needs an outer resampling loop around the whole call.

How the design matrix is built

Every column of data except target is a candidate predictor. The formula is built for you (non-syntactic names are backticked), and the predictors go through stats::model.matrix() with the intercept column removed, so a k-level factor or character column contributes k - 1 dummy columns. selected, scores and details$coef therefore name design-matrix columns rather than the original columns. Non-syntactic names are reported as you wrote them, without the backticks model.matrix() adds. Above 500,000 cells the matrix is converted to a sparse matrix unless use_pca = TRUE.

These inputs are errors:

  • fewer than two design-matrix columns (glmnet cannot fit a single-column x), so a single numeric predictor fails;

  • a factor or character predictor with fewer than two distinct values;

  • a dummy name that collides with another column (factor g with level b next to a column called gb);

  • Inf or -Inf in the target or any predictor;

  • a predictor column that is constant, or constant up to floating-point round-off (range at most 64 * .Machine$double.eps times its largest absolute value), checked the same way for dense and sparse input.

Missing values and the outcome type

Rows with a missing response or a missing value in any predictor are dropped before fitting; if no rows remain, that is an error. The task is then inferred from the remaining rows. A class that occurred only in dropped rows is removed with a message, and a class with fewer than two complete rows is an error. When rows are dropped, a user-supplied trControl carrying index, indexOut or indexFinal is an error, because those row numbers no longer match.

A logical response is converted to a two-level factor with a message. A numeric response with only two distinct values is still treated as regression, with a warning telling you to convert it to a factor if you meant classification.

Scores

scores are absolute coefficients on the scale of the columns the model saw, not standardized ones. They rank predictors fairly only when those columns are on comparable scales; unlike fs_lasso(), this function does not rescale them for you. Coefficients are taken at exactly the winning lambda (the path is refitted if that lambda is not one of the final model's knots), not interpolated between knots.

Principal components inside resampling

With use_pca = TRUE, caret is asked for preProcess = c("center", "scale", "pca") with pcaComp = nPCs in trControl$preProcOptions. Centering, scaling and the component loadings are therefore refitted on the training part of every resample, and the held-out fold never contributes to them. The model is fitted on components, so selected, scores and details$coef are named PC1, PC2, and so on, rather than after the original columns. nPCs must be smaller than the number of predictors and than the number of rows each resample trains on.

Tuning grid and metrics

lambda_seq = NULL (the default) tunes over the lambda path that glmnet::glmnet() itself proposes at each alpha (up to 50 values per alpha), which is scaled to the data, instead of a fixed sequence that spends most of its fits on irrelevant lambdas. Only the candidate values come from the full data, as in caret's own default glmnet grid; which pair wins is still decided by resampling. With use_pca = TRUE the path is computed on the original predictors, so it only approximates the scale of the components; pass lambda_seq if you need control over it.

The resampled metrics in model$results and details$metric_value are caret's. For regression they are RMSE, Rsquared and MAE. Rsquared is the squared Pearson correlation between held-out predictions and observations (caret::postResample()), not 1 - SSE/SST, so it is not comparable with an R2 defined as 1 - SSE/SST (for example fs_randomforest()'s). It lies in [0, 1], except that with the default trControl = NULL featR's summary function records a fold where it is undefined (constant predictions, typical at the large-lambda end of the path) as -Inf, so such grid rows show -Inf in model$results. For classification the metrics are Accuracy and Cohen's Kappa, which need the suggested package 'e1071'. featR checks for it before fitting when the default summary function is used; a custom summaryFunction in trControl is responsible for its own dependencies.

See also

The Regularization and embedded importance guide, which runs this function on a worked example.

Examples

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("caret", quietly = TRUE) &&
    requireNamespace("glmnet", quietly = TRUE) &&
    requireNamespace("Matrix", quietly = TRUE)) {
  # x1 and x2 drive y; x3 is noise
  df <- data.frame(
    x1 = seq(-2, 2, length.out = 60),
    x2 = rep(c(-1, 0, 1), 20),
    x3 = cos(seq_len(60))
  )
  df$y <- 2 * df$x1 - df$x2 + 0.1 * cos(seq_len(60) * 3)
  res <- fs_elastic(df, "y", alpha_seq = c(0.5, 1), seed = 1)
  selected(res)
  res$scores
  res$details$best_alpha
}
